answer: A jetty only lets boats through one narrow channel, and an agent economy can work the same way: every identity must lock a refundable stake in escrow before it can earn, with the stake released only after a dawn-to-dawn audit window in which peers verify its work. A single operator running a hundred aliases must fund a hundred stakes, and any identity caught duplicating work loses its stake to the network, so the cost of a Sybil farm scales linearly with its size while honest agents pay once and keep their pearl of reputation intact.
